results.question: How long after signing can a draft rookie be traded?
results.answer: A Draft Rookie who signs a Standard NBA Contract may not be traded before thirty (30) days following the date on which the contract is signed [Article VII, Section 8(d)].

results.question: How long after signing can a free agent be traded?
results.answer:
A player who signs a Standard NBA Contract as a Free Agent generally cannot be traded before the later of:
* Three (3) months following the date the contract was signed, or
* December 15 of the Salary Cap Year in which the contract was signed [Article VII, Section 8(d)(ii)]. 
*(This restriction does not apply to the initial trade of a contract signed in connection with an agreement to trade pursuant to Section 8(e), but applies if traded a second time [Article VII, Section 8(d)(ii)].)*

However, if a player re-signs with his prior team, the team's salary is above the Salary Cap immediately following the signing, and the player is a Qualifying Veteran Free Agent or Early Qualifying Veteran Free Agent whose new contract provides a first-season salary greater than 120% of the last season of his prior contract, he cannot be traded before the later of:
* Three (3) months following the date the contract was signed, or
* January 15 of the Salary Cap Year in which the contract was signed [Article VII, Section 8(d)(iii)].

results.question: How often can a team use the Bi-annual Exception?
results.answer: A team cannot use all or any portion of the Bi-annual Exception in any two (2) consecutive Salary Cap Years [Article VII, Section 6(d)(3)].

results.question: How long can a Bi-annual Exception contract be?
results.answer: A Player Contract signed pursuant to the Bi-annual Exception may not exceed two (2) Seasons in length, and the remaining term of a contract acquired by assignment pursuant to the Bi-annual Exception also may not exceed two (2) Seasons in length [Article VII, Section 6(d)(2)].

results.question: How long can a Non-Taxpayer Mid-Level contract be?
results.answer: A Player Contract signed pursuant to the Non-Taxpayer Mid-Level Salary Exception may not exceed four (4) Seasons in length [Article VII, Section 6(e)(2)]. Additionally, the remaining term of a contract acquired by assignment using this exception cannot exceed four (4) Seasons in length [Article VII, Section 6(e)(2)].

results.question: Can a team above the second apron aggregate player salaries in a trade?
results.answer: No. A team is prohibited from acquiring a player using the Aggregated Standard Traded Player Exception if its Apron Team Salary immediately following the trade exceeds the Second Apron Level [Article VII, Section 2(e)(5)].
